skill.name: ci-transit
skill.description: Visualize GitHub Actions runs as interactive transit maps, with jobs as lines, steps as stations, and timing and failure alerts.
skill.summary: Turn saved or fetched GitHub Actions runs into local interactive maps and optional GIF or MP4 exports.
skill.author: israelvicars

security_audit.summary: Most matches are syntax or legitimate tooling; confirmed risks include dependency lifecycle execution, contract-panel HTML injection, insecure credential transport, and predictable temporary files. Strict sharing can retain sensitive identifiers, and setup networking exceeds documented boundaries. The static cap leaves 245 matches unadjudicated, so manual review remains necessary. Static review was capped at 400/645 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 245 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Automatic setup executes downloaded dependency lifecycle scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit installation approval, ship a reviewed lockfile, use npm ci, and restrict lifecycle execution to audited packages.

remediation.issue: Contract confidence metadata reaches innerHTML without escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Validate contract indexes against a schema, enforce a confidence enum, and render metadata through escaped text or textContent.

remediation.issue: PostHog and Tempo adapters permit credentialed HTTP requests.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS for credentialed remote endpoints. Allow localhost HTTP only through an explicit development option and reject HTTPS downgrades.

remediation.issue: Screenshots use predictable shared temporary paths.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private temporary directory with mkdtemp, validate timestamp arguments, and avoid following existing output symlinks.

remediation.issue: Strict sharing preserves sensitive fallback identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Replace source identifiers with stable opaque identifiers and update references consistently before serializing shared output. Test jobs without databaseId.

remediation.issue: The stated network boundary omits setup downloads.
remediation.suggestion: Document registry, browser, and binary downloads separately from run fetching. Explain no-download controls and obtain approval before enabling installation.

remediation.issue: The static review cap excludes 245 matches.
remediation.suggestion: Complete manual review of the omitted matches before automatic publication. Retain the incomplete-coverage warning until that review is recorded.

content.user_title: Visualize GitHub Actions Runs as Transit Maps
content.value_statement: Long CI runs make failed steps and timing relationships difficult to review. This skill turns run metadata into interactive transit maps and optional visual exports.
actual_capabilities: Fetch a specific run or the latest failed run through the local GitHub CLI, with repository, workflow, and branch filters.
Build a self-contained HTML map with jobs as lines, steps as stations, timing details, and failure or cancellation alerts.
Apply key redaction and value scrubbing, with strict sharing mode and a failure-focused opening view.
Shorten idle gaps and collapse large runs to failed or cancelled step stations, with options to preserve full detail.
Render PNG frames, GIF animations, MP4 videos, and contact sheets through Chromium and ffmpeg.
Check repeated-render frame hashes, departure timing, and blank or frozen video segments using bundled verification scripts.
limitations: Requires Node.js 20 or later; fetching private runs also requires an authenticated GitHub CLI with appropriate access.
GIF and MP4 rendering require Chromium and ffmpeg; first-run setup can download dependencies and browser binaries.
Run metadata does not establish failure root causes; dependency links require supplied dependency metadata.
Scrubbing is heuristic and can retain sensitive identifiers; review every artifact before sharing outside its authorized audience.

use_cases.title: Inspect a Failed Pipeline
use_cases.description: Map a failed workflow run to identify unsuccessful steps and compare their timing with neighboring work.

use_cases.title: Review CI Scheduling
use_cases.description: Inspect job timing, idle periods, and supplied dependency links to discuss pipeline scheduling changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Incident Artifact
use_cases.description: Create a reviewed local HTML map or animation for an incident discussion without uploading private run data automatically.

prompt_templates.title: Map a Saved Run
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: use an existing local export.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use ci-transit to map ./run.json as a local HTML file. Identify failed or cancelled steps. Do not fetch data or install dependencies.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect the Latest Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Fetch the latest failed GitHub Actions run for [owner/repo] on [branch]. Build its map and report failed steps. Keep all outputs local.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Sharing Artifact
prompt_templates.prompt: Build ./run.json with strict sharing mode into ./transit-out/review.html. Check identifiers and visible labels for sensitive data. Report the verdict without uploading anything.

prompt_templates.title: Render and Verify Full Timing
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: preserve detail and verify media.
prompt_templates.prompt: Render ./run.json with every step and uncompressed timing. Ask before downloading dependencies. Export GIF and MP4, run bundled verification, and report paths and failures.

output_examples.input: Map a saved run containing a failed unit-test step.
output: Interactive HTML map created locally, with each job represented as a line.
The failed unit-test step is marked with a service alert and selectable timing details.

output_examples.input: Render a large run with a long idle period using default settings.
output: The map indicates that only failed or cancelled step stations are shown.
Long idle periods are shortened, and the page labels the compressed timing.
Full step detail and wall-clock timing remain available through explicit build options.

output_examples.input: Create and verify an animation from a synthetic CI sample.
output: Local GIF, MP4, and contact-sheet files are generated when rendering dependencies are available.
Verification reports frame reproducibility, departure timing, and blank or frozen segment checks.
Failed checks are reported without claiming the render passed.

best_practices: Use synthetic runs for demonstrations and review strict-mode output, including identifiers, before sharing.
Choose dedicated output directories and approve dependency downloads before rendering on restricted machines.
Preserve all steps and wall-clock timing when investigating delays; use compressed views only for presentation.
anti_patterns: Assuming automatic redaction guarantees that every private value is removed.
Uploading private CI artifacts or expanding access without explicit authorization.
Treating service alerts or compressed animation duration as a complete root-cause analysis.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Its bundled commands run locally through Node.js.

faq.question: Do I need GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Only fetching requires GitHub CLI. A compatible saved run file can be mapped without it.

faq.question: Does the generated HTML need an internet connection?
faq.answer: The standard generated page embeds its data, code, and fonts. Fetching and first-run rendering setup can require network access.

faq.question: Are GIF and MP4 exports available?
faq.answer: Yes. Rendering uses Chromium and ffmpeg, which must be available locally or installed through approved setup.

faq.question: Does strict sharing remove every secret?
faq.answer: No. Strict mode removes many sensitive patterns, but identifiers can retain private values. Inspect the complete artifact before sharing.

faq.question: Why are steps missing or timings shortened?
faq.answer: Large runs default to failed or cancelled step stations, and long idle gaps are compressed. Explicit options restore all steps and wall-clock timing.
